questions.q: How does this lesson relate availability, Business Continuity Planning (BCP), and Disaster Recovery (DR) to each other?
options: They are unrelated, independent concepts with no connection to each other
DR is a technical component supporting BCP's broader goal, and availability is the day-to-day baseline both are ultimately protecting
Availability is a subset of DR, which is itself a subset of a single vendor's uptime guarantee
BCP only applies to IT systems and has no broader organizational scope
questions.explain: The lesson nests these concepts: DR is the specific technical restoration plan supporting BCP's broader organizational continuity goal, with everyday availability as the baseline both ultimately protect.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does Salesforce publish that it maintains for its own cloud services?
options: Nothing -- Salesforce makes no public statement about its own resilience programs
Business Continuity Planning and Disaster Recovery programs, reviewed against industry standards and regulatory requirements, with separate published materials for different infrastructure
A guarantee that customers never need their own backup strategy
A commitment to notify every customer individually before any infrastructure maintenance
questions.explain: Salesforce publishes that it maintains BCP and DR programs for its cloud services, reviewed against industry standards and regulatory requirements, with separate DR materials covering different infrastructure such as Hyperforce and first-party AWS hosting.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Salesforce's own infrastructure resilience program does NOT eliminate an enterprise's need for its own backup and recovery planning?
options: Because infrastructure DR protects against Salesforce's own systems failing, while a backup product protects against the enterprise's own mistakes, like an accidental bulk delete or a bad data load
Because Salesforce has no infrastructure resilience program of any kind
Because backup products are only relevant to on-premises systems, never to SaaS platforms
Because Disaster Recovery and backup are simply two names for the exact same thing
questions.explain: The lesson draws a clear line: infrastructure-level DR protects the Salesforce platform itself from Salesforce's own failures, while a backup product protects against the enterprise's self-inflicted or integration-inflicted data problems -- two genuinely different risks.

questions.q: What does this lesson say an enterprise's availability planning has to account for, beyond Salesforce's own platform resilience?
options: Nothing further -- once Salesforce's resilience program is confirmed, no other planning is needed
The availability of every other system in the landscape, since an end-to-end process is only as available as its least available critical dependency
Only the availability of the company's internal network hardware
Availability planning is solely the responsibility of each individual end user
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that a landscape is only as available, for any given business process, as its least available critical dependency -- so availability planning has to span every system in the chain, not just Salesforce.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is Salesforce's Backup and Recover product described as offering?
options: Real-time infrastructure failover between data centers
Scheduled daily backups and on-demand snapshots covering data, metadata, files, and attachments
A replacement for Salesforce's own Disaster Recovery program
A tool exclusively for encrypting fields at rest
questions.explain: The lesson describes Backup and Recover as Salesforce's customer-facing product offering scheduled daily backups plus on-demand snapshots of data, metadata, files, and attachments -- a separate concern from platform-level infrastructure DR.
